answer: A market buying nectar forecasts on a knoll requires each agent to carry a signed performance policy for its crystal sensor. An independent underwriter locks collateral per active policy and groups accounts sharing a sensor or funding source under one exposure limit. Fifty aliases need fifty policies, premiums and locked reserves; fabricated readings trigger claims against the underwriter. Attackers must finance more real sensors or persuade more underwriters to risk capital. Colluding underwriters could certify a sham fleet, so random field audits and public claim records are needed.
